fields.statement: Built 4df6a76b into a scratch binary. In a scratch repo, a source added with --json-field quotes as plain strings ['We must  keep\nit small, always.','We shall grow later.','Cheap is fine: must keep it lean too? no'] and decision small (quote 'must keep it') derived from it: rhiza why small printed only the two matching quotes and 'Quotes left out: 1', --json quotes_left_out 1. But on this repo's own model, rhiza why name-is-genesis / go-one-binary / six-layers still print all 40 quotes of founding-conversation (235 lines, quotes_left_out 0), though name-is-genesis's quote 'yes, Genesis it is, move on to the log format' is the text of exactly one of them: sources written by rhiza source add store quotes as objects {text,by,where}, and whyCitedQuotes unmarshals quotes only as []string, so it never trims a real source. Also rhiza why c2 for a capability decided by two decisions citing different quotes of one source showed the source once, trimmed to the first decision's quotes, hiding the second decision's cited quote.

Built 4df6a76b into a scratch binary; in a scratch repo with a three-string-quote source: rhiza why on a decision whose quote matches nothing, a decision with no quote, and a capability derived from the source each printed all three quotes with no 'Quotes left out' line and quotes_left_out 0 in --json; a trimmed decision printed 'Quotes left out: 1' in text and quotes_left_out 1 in --json. go test ./internal/api -run TestWhy and TestScripts/(why|describe-golden) pass.
